task.name: Deployment Drift Remediation
task.description: Review production deployment configuration after approved infrastructure changes and surface only services whose committed deployment manifests no longer match the active cluster configuration.
task.intent: Reduce operator time spent discovering and correcting production deployment drift after approved changes without reopening services whose drift is already tracked or intentionally accepted.
activationConditions: A merged pull request within the evidence window changes deployment manifests, Helm values, or environment configuration for a production service.
Authoritative deployment evidence shows at least one active production service differs materially from the committed configuration after the change.
requiredEffects: Each novel drift finding identifies the affected service, the authoritative deployment evidence, and the mismatched configuration dimension.
Maintainers can accept, reject, or resolve each surfaced finding using repository-linked evidence.
noopConditions: No changed production service differs materially between committed configuration and authoritative deployment evidence.
Every supported drift finding for the changed services is already tracked or explicitly accepted.
successConditions: Supported drift findings receive accepted remediation evidence or an explicit maintainer dismissal within the evidence window.
Changes whose deployments already match committed configuration create no duplicate maintainer attention.
uncertainties: Some production overrides may be intentionally managed outside the repository but still documented as accepted drift.
One infrastructure change can create several service-specific drift findings that share the same source pull request.

operationalValue.statement: The proportion of supported, novel deployment-drift findings assigned to the run that are resolved or explicitly dismissed within 14 days.
operationalValue.opportunity: One workflow run and the deduplicated supported deployment-drift findings it assigns for the changed production services.
acceptedEvidence: A merged pull request that restores the affected production service's committed deployment manifest, Helm values, or environment configuration to match authoritative deployment evidence.
A closed tracking issue or pull request conversation that explicitly marks the drift finding resolved, dismissed, or intentionally accepted by a maintainer.
evidenceRepositories: The repository in which the workflow ran.

metric.name: resolved-supported-drift-findings
metric.formula: resolved-or-dismissed supported drift findings / supported novel drift findings assigned to the run

operationalValue.maturation: 14 days after the workflow run completes.
operationalValue.zeroRule: Return 0 when at least one supported novel drift finding was assigned and none has accepted resolution evidence by the evidence cutoff.
operationalValue.missingRule: Return null when the assigned drift finding set or required repository evidence for the changed production services cannot be read.
